title.narrative: EC Ibarra Transport Infrastructure Improvement Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve mobility of Ibarra and the use of recreational spaces in the Yahuarcocha lagoon area, and to respond effectively in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency

The development objective of the Ibarra Transport Infrastructure Improvement Project for Ecuador is to improve mobility in Ibarra and the use of recreational spaces in the Yahuarcocha Lagoon area. The project comprises of four components. The first component, improve mobility in the city will improve traffic flows by providing better access to the city center and mobility for through traffic and relieve congestion within the city center (including the historic core) by providing an alternate path for through traffic. The second component, improve public and tourist spaces will improve the quality and quantity of public space, including outdoor, recreational, and tourist-friendly public space. The third component, technical assistance will provide technical assistance to support units in the municipality of Ibarra that are responsible for mobility, public works, traffic, urban transport, and urban planning. The fourth component, project management will finance targeted incremental costs associated with overall project management, including project-related audits, monitoring and evaluation (M and E) to track progress on project indicators, environmental and social management, beneficiary assessments, feedback mechanisms, procurement, training, and staffing, including a project coordinator.

title.narrative: Progress of construction and restoration of tourist spaces works on Yahuarcocha Boulevard

comment.narrative: Planned investments in Yahuarcocha lagoon recreational area have been completed (Component 2). Construction work began in August 2017 and concluded in October 2019.

title.narrative: Share of Project beneficiaries expressing satisfaction with the Ring Boulevard infrastructure and mobility options

comment.narrative:
This indicator assesses the satisfaction level of beneficiaries with the construction of the NRR infrastructure and the new mobility options provided post-Project implementation. The satisfaction survey, conducted between October and November 2024, targeted a diverse sample of 274 individuals. This sample was designed to ensure representation across various demographic factors, including gender, age, occupation, and income levels. Key points highlighted in the survey include improved accessibility, reduced travel time, enhanced city integration, and noticeable visual improvements.
This indicator does not measure satisfaction with the SRR as it has not been constructed.

title.narrative: Number of people in Azaya-Alpachaca neighborhood who can access the city center by public transport in 25 minutes or less.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of people in the Azaya-Alpachaca neighborhood (north-west) who can access the city center by public transport in 25 minutes or less. The count of individuals with improved access increased from 1,683 to 7,367.

title.narrative: Percentage of visitors who use a bicycle and walk in Yahuarcocha

comment.narrative: The baseline measurement in April 2017 showed that 18% of visitors used bicycles and walked in Yahuarocha. The percentage of visitors who use bicycles and walk in Yahuarcocha increased to 45%.

title.narrative: Average travel time by private transport to area hospitals from select low-income areas influenced by the Ring Road.

comment.narrative: This indicator assesses the travel time between the San Antonio neighborhood (south-west) and the Ibarra Public Hospital (north-west). Travel time using the NRR was found to be 24.01 minutes less compared to the traditional route (34.11 minutes vs. 10.1 minutes).

title.narrative: Number of yearly visitors to Yahuarcocha

comment.narrative: Between October 2022 and September 2023, a total of 247,300 vehicles accessed Yahuarcocha Lagoon. With an estimated average occupancy rate of 1.5 passengers per vehicle, this equates to approximately 370,950 visitors arriving by car. Considering that visitors entering Yahuarcocha Lagoon account for approximately 45% of the total (as indicated by PDO indicator 2), an estimated additional 303,505 visitors must be added. Therefore, the annual total number of visitors to Yahuarcocha is approximately 674,455.

In October 2018, the Municipality of Ibarra established an organizational structure outlined in the implementation agreements, which were subsequently updated by municipal resolutions in December 2019 and November 2020. The Project optimizes the utilization of existing capacities within the Municipality of Ibarra. Technical specialists report directly to the Project Coordinator, who serves as the main liaison with the Director of Public Works and the contract administrator.
However, as of February 2024, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) has undergone significant downsizing. The Director of Public Works now manages the two remaining consulting contracts, while the Project Coordinator is supported by only one financial specialist and one environmental specialist. Currently, there has been non-compliance with the Operations Manual.

title.narrative: Study for the improvement of sustainable mobility in Ibarra prepared

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures progress in two TAs: (a) Study for the restructuring of the public transport system (US$642,724). The primary beneficiary agency is Movildelnor, the transport agency responsible for planning in Ibarra and neighboring cities. This consultancy is currently under implementation, and according to the Borrower, it is expected to conclude by the project's closing date. (b) Study of urban planning, heritage, and tourism management (US$569,976). The primary beneficiary agency is the Ibarra Department of Planning and has been successfully completed.
Both TAs are critical inputs to fulfilling a key covenant of the project in the LA: The Borrower shall execute the project in accordance with the POM, which includes rules, methods, guidelines, standard documents, and procedures for carrying out the Project. This includes measures to ensure proper land use in the areas adjacent to the RB and measures to facilitate the incorporation of new bus routes through the RB.

This indicator tracks progress in TA: Development of a road asset management and maintenance system (US$784,675). The primary beneficiary of this TA is the Ibarra Department of Works and Construction and has been successfully completed. This activity is crucial for ensuring the sustainability of mobility improvements through the implementation of an effective road asset management system.

title.narrative: People with enhanced access to transportation services

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the project's impact within a 300-meter radius of the NRR and SRR. It combines the number of households and the average household size to estimate the number of beneficiaries.
It's important to highlight that the current data does not capture the impact of the SRR because this segment has not been constructed. Although this intermediate indicator includes potential beneficiaries from the SRR, there is no data to report. As a result, the current data does not fully meet the end target.

The NRR, covering approximately 9.5 km, has been successfully completed and is now open to traffic. The SRR was excluded from the project's result framework during the restructuring approved in May 2021.
An Alternative Study was commissioned to assess the connection of the NRR to Yahuarcocha Lagoon, (involving the construction of 1.9 km of new road, including a 400-meter bridge), as well as improving the technical design of the SRR (approximately 12 km). However, these infrastructure projects will not be implemented within the scope of this project.

title.narrative: Share of business owners in Yahuarcocha Lagoon business area whose monthly income level is at or exceeds the minimum wage

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the proportion of business owners whose monthly income level meets or exceeds the minimum wage ($386). The baseline measurement in April 2017, when the minimum wage was $375, indicated that 45 percent of business owners had incomes above the minimum wage. At completion, this share increased to 68.12 percent.
